title: Commercial Loan Application Narrative - Credit Evaluation Rubric

scale.meaning: 5 = strongest / lowest risk, 1 = weakest / highest risk. Use N/E when the narrative provides no evidence either way.

rubrics.name: Character
rubrics.question: Does the borrower demonstrate the willingness and integrity to repay?

levels.5: Clean credit across all principals (FICO 740+). 5+ years relevant industry experience. No liens, judgments, or litigation. Disclosure complete and unprompted.
levels.4: Strong credit (FICO 680-739) with any past blemish fully explained and resolved. Solid experience. Minor historical item disclosed proactively.
levels.3: Acceptable credit (FICO 620-679) or a limited ownership track record. Some late payments in the last 24 months. Disclosure adequate but required follow-up.
levels.2: Weak credit (FICO below 620), recent delinquencies, an open lien or judgment, or thin management experience. Gaps in disclosure.
levels.1: Bankruptcy, charge-off, or unresolved judgment within 3 years; evidence of misrepresentation; or principals evasive on material facts.

rubrics.name: Capacity
rubrics.question: Does cash flow cover the proposed debt service?
rubrics.primary_metric: DSCR = Adjusted EBITDA / Total Annual Debt Service

levels.5: DSCR 1.35x or better. Revenue growing year over year. Add-backs minimal and well documented.
levels.4: DSCR 1.25x - 1.34x. Revenue stable to growing. Add-backs reasonable.
levels.3: DSCR 1.15x - 1.24x. Revenue flat. Coverage adequate but with little cushion.
levels.2: DSCR 1.00x - 1.14x. Revenue declining, or coverage depends heavily on aggressive add-backs.
levels.1: DSCR below 1.00x. Cash flow does not cover the proposed debt service.

rubrics.hard_rule: A score of 1 on Capacity triggers an automatic DECLINE regardless of the weighted total.

rubrics.name: Capital
rubrics.question: How much of the borrower's own money is at risk?
rubrics.primary_metric: Equity injection as a percentage of total project cost

levels.5: Equity injection 25% or more of total project cost. Strong tangible net worth. Six or more months of operating reserves.
levels.4: Equity injection 20% - 24%. Healthy net worth. Three to six months of reserves.
levels.3: Equity injection 15% - 19%. Adequate net worth. One to three months of reserves.
levels.2: Equity injection 10% - 14%. Thin net worth or negligible reserves.
levels.1: Equity injection below 10%, negative tangible net worth, or no meaningful liquidity.

rubrics.name: Collateral
rubrics.question: What is the secondary source of repayment if cash flow fails?

levels.5: LTV 65% or less. First lien on readily marketable collateral. Appraisal within 12 months. Unlimited personal guarantees from all principals.
levels.4: LTV 66% - 75%. First lien. Appraisal current. Guarantees in place.
levels.3: LTV 76% - 80%. First lien but collateral is specialized or slower to liquidate.
levels.2: LTV 81% - 90%, subordinate lien position, or illiquid / single-purpose collateral.
levels.1: LTV above 90%, effectively unsecured, no current valuation, or no guarantees.

rubrics.name: Conditions
rubrics.question: Do the loan purpose, industry, and market environment support repayment?

levels.5: Growing, stable industry. No concentration above 20%. Use of proceeds specific and documented. Term well matched to asset life.
levels.4: Stable industry. Concentration 20% - 30%. Sound, clearly stated purpose.
levels.3: Mixed or cyclical industry outlook, or single-customer concentration 30% - 40%. Purpose acceptable.
levels.2: Declining industry, concentration above 40%, or loan term materially longer than the useful life of the asset financed.
levels.1: Distressed sector, use of proceeds unclear or shifting, or unresolved regulatory / environmental liability.

scoring_method.no_evidence: Score a criterion N/E when the narrative is silent on it. N/E is not a low score: the criterion earns no points AND its weight is removed from the denominator, so the total is renormalised over the weight that was actually evidenced. Never score silence as 1 - level 1 describes a documented weakness, not an absent section.
scoring_method.total: total = (points earned / weight evidenced) * 100, rounded half up to a whole number. When every C is scored the denominator is 100 and this is a plain sum. When a C is N/E the denominator shrinks by that C's weight.
scoring_method.worked_example_with_ne: C1 4/20, C2 4/30, C3 3/20, C5 3/10 earn 16 + 24 + 12 + 6 = 58 points. C4 is N/E, so its weight of 20 leaves the denominator: 58 / 80 * 100 = 72.5, which rounds to 73 - APPROVE WITH CONDITIONS.
scoring_method.rounding: Round half up, so 72.5 becomes 73. Do not use banker's rounding.
scoring_method.order_of_operations: Compute the total, find its decision band, and only then apply the hard rules. A hard rule overrides the band it lands in.

decision_bands.note: Meets policy on all five C's. Proceed to documentation.
Sound credit with identified weaknesses. Approve subject to covenants addressing the lowest-scoring rubrics.
Material weaknesses. Requires senior review, restructure, or additional support before a decision.
Does not meet minimum underwriting standards.

hard_rules.reason: DSCR below 1.00x. The loan does not cover its own debt service; collateral strength does not substitute for repayment capacity.
